Section 1 · Fundamentals

What chemistry and physics decide how this reactor behaves?

Section 1 · the plan

Five ideas carry the whole unit

  1. The reaction and its heathow much hydrogen and heat one tonne of benzene means
  2. Equilibriumwhy the reactors stay below about 250 °C
  3. Kinetics and hydrogen partial pressurewhat the rate actually depends on
  4. Vapour pressure and evaporative coolingwhy R-101 “boils its own product”
  5. Reactor balancesmole and energy balances for a stirred tank and a packed bed

1 · The reaction and its heat

One reaction, very exothermicstep 1 of 3

$$\mathrm{C_6H_6} + 3\,\mathrm{H_2} \;\longrightarrow\; \mathrm{C_6H_{12}} \qquad \Delta H_r \approx -206\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$$
$\mathrm{C_6H_6}$
benzene, the liquid feed (99.9 %)
78.11 kg/kmol
$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}$
cyclohexane, the product
84.16 kg/kmol
$\Delta H_r$
heat of reaction per mol of benzene (negative = released)
kJ/mol

Nickel catalyst: Raney-Ni powder in the stirred reactors, supported Ni in the fixed bed.

1 · The reaction and its heat

What one tonne of benzene meansstep 2 of 3

From the previous slide$\mathrm{C_6H_6} + 3\,\mathrm{H_2} \to \mathrm{C_6H_{12}}$, $\;\Delta H_r=-206$ kJ/mol
$n_B = \dfrac{1000\ \mathrm{kg}}{78.11\ \mathrm{kg/kmol}} = 12.8\ \mathrm{kmol}$moles in one tonne
$m_{H_2} = 3 \times 12.8 \times 2.016 = 77.4\ \mathrm{kg}$three H₂ per benzene
$Q = 12.8\times10^{3} \times 206 = 2.64\ \mathrm{GJ}$heat released per tonne

At the design feed of 34.8 t/h this is 25.5 MW — the heat-removal problem of the whole unit.

1 · The reaction and its heat

Why heat removal is the heart of the designstep 3 of 3

$c_p$
molar heat capacity of the liquid (model value)
200 kJ/(kmol·K)
$\Delta T_{ad}$
temperature rise if no heat left the reactor
K
$$\Delta T_{ad} = \frac{-\Delta H_r}{c_p} = \frac{206\,000}{200} \approx 1000\ \mathrm{K}$$

Physically impossible — the liquid boils first. The number shows how much heat must leave continuously.

2 · Equilibrium

How far can the reaction go?step 1 of 2

The heat says keep it cool. Equilibrium says the same, for a different reason.

$K_p$
equilibrium constant, gas-phase basis
bar⁻³
$y_B,\ y_C$
mole fractions of benzene and cyclohexane
—
$p_{H_2}$
hydrogen partial pressure
bar
$\Delta G^\circ$
standard Gibbs energy of reaction, −97.9 kJ/mol at 298 K
kJ/mol
$$K_p=\frac{y_C}{y_B\,p_{H_2}^3}=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\Delta G^\circ}{RT}\right)$$

2 · Equilibrium

Temperature shifts the equilibrium backstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$K_p=\dfrac{y_C}{y_B\,p_{H_2}^3}$
$\ln K_p(T)=\ln K_{298}-\dfrac{\Delta H_r}{R}\left(\dfrac1T-\dfrac1{298}\right)$van ’t Hoff, ΔH assumed constant
$\dfrac{y_B}{y_C}\Big|_{eq}=\dfrac{1}{K_p\,p_{H_2}^3}$rearranged: benzene left at equilibrium

Exothermic: $K_p$ falls as $T$ rises. $\ln K_{298}=39.5$ from $\Delta G^\circ$.

Interactive — equilibrium

Where equilibrium starts to cost product quality

From the previous slide$\dfrac{y_B}{y_C}=\dfrac{1}{K_p\,p_{H_2}^3}$
Benzene at equilibrium

At 200 °C equilibrium leaves under 0.1 ppm; near 250 °C it reaches the 10 ppm spec — the reactors stay cool for quality, not only safety.

3 · Kinetics

The rate law used in the simulatorstep 1 of 3

$$r = k(T)\,a\,\varphi\,\frac{x_B}{K_B+x_B}\,p_{H_2}$$
$r$
benzene reacted per unit time
kmol/s
$k(T)$
Arrhenius rate constant, $E=55$ kJ/mol
kmol/(s·bar)
$a,\ \varphi$
catalyst activity × amount; mixing factor (agitator)
—
$x_B,\ K_B$
benzene mole fraction in liquid; saturation constant 0.03
—

3 · Kinetics

Two regimes hidden in one expressionstep 2 of 3

Rate law$r = k\,a\,\varphi\,\dfrac{x_B}{K_B+x_B}\,p_{H_2}$
$x_B \gg K_B:\quad r \approx k\,a\,\varphi\,p_{H_2}$R-101: rate set by hydrogen
$x_B \ll K_B:\quad r \approx \dfrac{k\,a\,\varphi}{K_B}\,x_B\,p_{H_2}$last ppm: first order in benzene

So R-101 is hydrogen-limited, and the finishing reactors are benzene-limited.

3 · Kinetics

Hydrogen partial pressure has three leversstep 3 of 3

$P$
reactor pressure (absolute)
bar a
$P_{sat}(T)$
cyclohexane vapour pressure at reactor temperature
bar
$y_{H_2}$
H₂ fraction of the dry gas in the reactor (78 % at R-101 outlet)
—
$$p_{H_2} = \big(P - P_{sat}(T)\big)\;y_{H_2}$$

A hotter reactor raises $k$ but lowers $p_{H_2}$ — the vapour takes up part of the pressure.

Interactive — what speeds up R-101?

Pressure, temperature and purity against the rate

Section 1 · step 3$p_{H_2}=(P-P_{sat})\,y_{H_2}$
Vapour pressure $P_{sat}$
Hydrogen partial pressure $p_{H_2}$
Rate constant $k/k_{200}$
Rate relative to design

Above about 225 °C extra temperature buys little rate because $P_{sat}$ eats the hydrogen pressure — purity and pressure are the cleaner levers.

3 · Kinetics

Hydrogen must reach the catalyst first

$k_La$
gas–liquid transfer coefficient × bubble area
s⁻¹
$C^*_{H_2}$
saturation H₂ in liquid, ∝ $p_{H_2}$ (Henry)
kmol/m³
$$N_{H_2}=k_La\,(C^*_{H_2}-C_{H_2})$$

Agitator or gas lost → $k_La$ collapses → rate collapses, whatever the temperature.

4 · Evaporative cooling

Cyclohexane vapour pressurestep 1 of 3

$P_{sat}$ appeared in $p_{H_2}$. It also sets the second cooling path of R-101.

$$\ln P_{sat}\,[\mathrm{bar}] = 10.256 - \frac{3625}{T\,[\mathrm{K}]}$$

Clausius–Clapeyron form fitted for the model; benzene treated alike.

$P_{sat}(200\,{}^\circ\mathrm C)=e^{10.256-3625/473.15}=13.4\ \mathrm{bar}$almost half the reactor pressure
$T_b(31\ \mathrm{bar\,a}) = \dfrac{3625}{10.256-\ln 31}-273 = 258\,{}^\circ\mathrm C$boiling point: a hard ceiling

4 · Evaporative cooling

The gas leaves saturated with vapourstep 2 of 3

$G$
non-condensable gas leaving R-101 (H₂ + inerts)
kmol/s
$V$
cyclohexane vapour carried with it
kmol/s
$\lambda$
latent heat of vaporisation (21 MJ/kmol at 200 °C)
kJ/kmol
$\dfrac{V}{G+V}=\dfrac{P_{sat}}{P}$vapour fraction = partial-pressure ratio
$V = G\,\dfrac{P_{sat}}{P-P_{sat}},\qquad Q_{boil}=\lambda V$solved for V; heat carried away

4 · Evaporative cooling

At design: the reactor boils away 3.3 MWstep 3 of 3

From the previous slide$V = G\,\dfrac{P_{sat}}{P-P_{sat}}$,   $Q_{boil}=\lambda V$
$V = 745 \times \dfrac{13.4}{31-13.4} = 567\ \mathrm{kmol/h}$G = 745 kmol/h at design
$Q_{boil} = \dfrac{567}{3600}\times 21\,200 = 3.3\ \mathrm{MW}$E-103 condenses it as reflux

Hotter → larger $P_{sat}$ → more boil-up: R-101 partly regulates itself.

Interactive — boiling its own product

Boil-up per mole of gas rises steeply near the ceiling

Section 1 · step 2$\dfrac{V}{G}=\dfrac{P_{sat}}{P-P_{sat}}$
$V/G$
Boiling point $T_b$

Lowering the pressure moves the ceiling down and multiplies boil-up — pressure sets how hard R-101 can cool itself.

5 · Reactor balances

Mole balance of a stirred tank (CSTR)step 1 of 3

Rate and heat are known. The reactor type decides how far the rate can take the benzene.

$F_{B0}$
benzene fed
kmol/s
$X$
fractional conversion of benzene
—
$Da$
Damköhler number: rate constant × residence time
—
$0 = F_{B0}(1-X) - F_{B0} + r$steady state: in − out − consumed = 0
$X_{CSTR} = \dfrac{Da}{1+Da}$with first-order $r$ at outlet concentration

5 · Reactor balances

Plug flow and tanks in seriesstep 2 of 3

From the previous slide$X_{CSTR}=\dfrac{Da}{1+Da}$
$X_{PFR} = 1-e^{-Da}$integrating along the bed (R-103)
$X_{N\,\mathrm{tanks}} = 1-\left(1+\dfrac{Da}{N}\right)^{-N}$N equal tanks in series

A CSTR runs at its outlet concentration — the slowest point of the curve.

Interactive — why three reactors?

Benzene left after one tank, two tanks or a bed

Section 1 · step 2$1-X_{CSTR}=\dfrac{1}{1+Da}$
$1-X_{PFR}=e^{-Da}$
1 CSTR
2 CSTRs
Plug flow

A single tank needs $Da\approx 5\times10^5$ for 2 ppm; plug flow needs 13 — so the bulk reacts in tanks, the ppm in a bed.

5 · Reactor balances

Energy balance of R-101step 3 of 3

$$0 = r\,(-\Delta H_r) - Q_{feed} - Q_{gas} - Q_{boil} - Q_{reflux} - Q_{E101} - Q_{loss}$$
$Q_{feed},\,Q_{gas}$
heating benzene (40 °C) and hydrogen (60 °C) to 200 °C
MW
$Q_{boil},\,Q_{reflux}$
boiling vapour off; reheating the returned condensate
MW
$Q_{E101}$
pump-around cooler — the only adjustable term
MW

Design: 25.0 = 4.0 + 2.4 + 3.3 + 4.4 + 9.6 + 1.2 MW.

Section 1

What section 1 settled

  • Each tonne of benzene needs 77 kg of H₂ and releases 2.6 GJ: heat removal is the design problem.
  • Equilibrium is complete below ~250 °C; above it, benzene returns.
  • R-101 is hydrogen-limited: $p_{H_2}=(P-P_{sat})\,y_{H_2}$ and mixing set the rate.
  • The gas carries vapour away: $V=G\,P_{sat}/(P-P_{sat})$ — R-101 boils its own product.
  • Tanks do the bulk, the packed bed the last ppm.

The equations are in hand. Section 2 uses them to size the reactors and their cooling.

Two product specs set two limits

2 · Reactor volume

Liquid volume from residence timestep 1 of 2

$n_L$
moles of liquid held in the reactor
kmol
$\rho_L$
molar liquid density, $9.3-0.0105\,T$
kmol/m³
$V_L$

2 · Reactor volume

R-101 at designstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$V_L=n_L/\rho_L \qquad \tau=n_L/F_{B0}$
$\rho_L = 9.3-0.0105\times200 = 7.2\ \mathrm{kmol/m^3}$density at 200 °C
$V_L = 209/7.2 = 29\ \mathrm{m^3}$n = 209 kmol from the model
$\tau = 209/0.1238 = 1690\ \mathrm{s}\approx 28\ \mathrm{min}$F = 0.1238 kmol/s benzene

The vessel (50 m³ span) leaves room for gas hold-up and disengagement.

3 · Heat-removal design

Four paths carry 25 MW out of R-101

Sensible heat

Feed 40 → 200 °C and H₂ 60 → 200 °C: 6.4 MW

Boil-up + reflux

Vapour to E-103, cold reflux back: 7.8 MW

E-101 pump-around

Raises LP steam in D-101: 9.6 MW — adjustable

Losses

Shell losses net of agitator work: 1.2 MW

Only E-101 has a valve (FV-104). The other three follow the feed, gas rate and temperature.

Interactive — size the pump-around duty

What is left for E-101 when the other paths are set?

E-101 must remove

More hydrogen or a hotter reactor boils more product and unloads E-101 — the gas rate is a second cooling handle.

4 · Hydrogen loop

Why feed 4.2 mol of H₂ per mol of benzene?

Section 1 · kinetics$p_{H_2}=(P-P_{sat})\,y_{H_2}$    $V=G\,\dfrac{P_{sat}}{P-P_{sat}}$
  • Only 3 mol react: the excess keeps $p_{H_2}$ high at the R-101 outlet.
  • The leftover gas $G$ carries the boil-up — cooling without a valve.
  • The same gas feeds R-102 and R-103 in series.

4 · Purge design

Methane can only leave through the purgestep 1 of 2

$Q_{mu},\ Q_{pu}$
make-up and purge gas flows
kmol/h
$y_{I,mu}$
inerts (CH₄) in the make-up, 0.5 %
—
$C_{H_2}$
hydrogen consumed by reaction, $3F_B$
kmol/h
$Q_{pu}(1-y)=Q_{mu}\,y_{I,mu}$inert balance: in = out at steady state
$Q_{mu}(1-y_{I,mu})=C_{H_2}+Q_{pu}\,y$hydrogen balance, no leak

4 · Purge design

Purity follows from the purge flowstep 2 of 2

From the previous slide$Q_{pu}(1-y)=Q_{mu}\,y_{I,mu}$,   $Q_{mu}(1-y_{I,mu})=C_{H_2}+Q_{pu}\,y$
$y \approx \dfrac{Q_{pu}-C_{H_2}\,y_{I,mu}}{Q_{pu}\,(1+y_{I,mu})}$eliminate Q_mu; y_I,mu small
$y=\dfrac{90-1337\times0.005}{90\times1.005}=0.921$design purge 90 kmol/h

Matches AI-105 = 92.1 %. Halve the purge and purity drops to about 85 %.

Interactive — the purge trade-off

Purity bought with hydrogen

From the previous slide$y \approx \dfrac{Q_{pu}-C_{H_2}\,y_{I,mu}}{Q_{pu}(1+y_{I,mu})}$
Recycle purity
H₂ lost in purge

When the make-up carries more methane, only a larger purge holds purity above 85 % — and every extra Nm³ purged is hydrogen paid for.

Layers between an upset and a runaway

LayerIn this unit
Inherentboiling-point ceiling (258 °C); boil-up grows with temperature
ControlTIC-101 → FIC-104 cascade; PIC-105 on loop pressure
AlarmsTI-100 HI 210 °C, JI-101 LO, AI-105 LO, TI-103 HI

Section 2

What section 2 settled

  • The two specs split the job: conversion for benzene, temperature for MCP.
  • Two stirred tanks do the bulk; a plug-flow bed finishes to 2 ppm.
  • R-101 holds 29 m³ of liquid, 28 min of feed.
  • 25 MW leave by sensible heat, boil-up and the E-101 steam raiser — only E-101 has a valve.
  • Purity is set by the purge: $y\approx(Q_{pu}-C_{H_2}y_{I,mu})/Q_{pu}$.

The design fixes the equipment. Section 3 asks how an operator keeps it inside its window.

2 · Controlling the heat

What the cascade does when the feed rises

Only E-101 has a valve, so every heat disturbance ends at FV-104.

FIC-101 ↑→heat released ↑→TIC-101 sees T ↑→FIC-104 SP ↑→FV-104 opens→LP steam ↑
  • +10 % benzene: FIC-104 357 → 505 t/h, LP steam 14.7 → 19.5 t/h after 30 min.
  • Watch the valve, not only the temperature: above 90 % there is no margin left.

$$0.995\,FI_{106} - FI_{107}\,AI_{105} \;=\; 3\times\frac{FIC_{101}}{78.11}\times 22.4 + \text{losses}$$

A gap above about 3 % means low conversion or a leak.

Make-up above the reaction demand with conversion unchanged points to a leak; below it, to lost conversion — the balance separates the two.

4 · Product quality

The analyzer is late — plan for it

  • AI-103 / AI-104 are one gas chromatograph (GC): a result every 4 min, sampled 2 min earlier.
  • A change in R-101 reaches V-104 through R-102, R-103 and the separator hold-up: tens of minutes.
  • HS-115 sends product to TK-106 (sales) only on spec; otherwise to TK-107 (slop).

Route to slop first, then diagnose — off-spec product in the sales tank costs the most.

5 · Start-up

The start-up order follows the hazards

#StepBecause
1Nitrogen pressure-purge until O₂ < 1 %H₂ in air burns from 4 to 75 %
2Charge cyclohexane, start agitator, add catalystcover the impeller and the sparger
3Admit H₂, pressure to 29 bar g, start K-101gas and pressure before any reaction
4Heat R-101 on MP steam to ≥ 140 °Cbenzene must react as it arrives
5Permit benzene at 25 %, switch E-101 to COOLlight-off, then remove the heat
6Raise rate in steps; product to TK-106 on specE-101 must follow the heat

5 · Shutdown and rate changes

Stop benzene first, hydrogen last

Normal shutdown

Half rate → stop benzene → react out with H₂ (make-up falls) → product to slop → cool → stop K-101 → depressure → N₂ purge.

Rate changes

Steps of about 0.7 t/h every 2 min; move FIC-103 with the feed: $\;FIC_{103}=46\,000\times F/34.8$.

JI-101 low, M-101 shows RUNagitator coupling failedclose XV-101 at once
TI-103 jumps to ~200 °Ccooling-water failurecut feed, plan shutdown
AI-105 fallinginerts building upopen purge HIC-107
Make-up up, conversion unchangedhydrogen leakfind it; reduce pressure

Section 3

What section 3 settled

  • Hold R-101 at 195–205 °C: MCP above, benzene slip below, the trip at 220 °C.
  • Every heat disturbance ends at FV-104 — watch its opening.
  • Check make-up − purge H₂ against 3 × benzene: a gap means a leak or lost conversion.
  • Start-up order: inert, liquid, hydrogen, heat, then benzene; shutdown in reverse.

The operating moves need a map. Section 4 walks the process stream by stream.

What does each stream and vessel do at the design point?

Walking the flowsheet

1 · Block flow diagram

The unit on one page

Blue hydrocarbon · purple hydrogen-rich gas · red steam · teal water. Hydrogen flows R-101 → R-102 → R-103 in series. Click to enlarge.

2 · Reaction section

Feed, R-101 and its two coolers

  • P-100A/B pump 34.8 t/h of benzene through FIC-101 and SIS valve XV-101.
  • K-101 sparges 46 000 Nm³/h of hydrogen under agitator M-101.
  • E-103 condenses the boil-up; V-103 returns it as reflux.
  • P-101A/B circulate slurry through E-101, which raises LP steam in D-101.

2 · Finishing section

R-102, the catalyst filter and R-103

  • Slurry overflows R-101 → R-102 (LIC-101); the V-103 gas is sparged into R-102.
  • R-102 at 160 °C: jacket on MP steam, because the gas strips vapour.
  • P-102A/B push liquid through candle filter F-102A/B — catalyst stays behind.
  • R-103, a trickle bed, finishes to 2 ppm.

2 · Separation and recycle

V-104 splits product from recycle gas

  • E-106 cools the R-103 effluent to 45 °C with cooling water.
  • V-104 at 29 bar g: liquid to storage (LIC-104, HS-115), gas to K-101.
  • PIC-105 admits make-up hydrogen; HIC-107 purges to fuel gas.

Pick a stream number from the diagram

The recycle gas (10) outweighs the make-up (11) five to one in moles — K-101 moves the hydrogen, the make-up only replaces what reacts or is purged.

5 · Following the benzene

R-103 as five cells in series

$x_k$
benzene leaving cell $k$ of the bed
ppm
$\kappa$
cell Damköhler number: activity × rate × residence
—
$$x_{k+1}=\frac{x_k}{1+\kappa}\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad x_{out}=\frac{x_{in}}{(1+\kappa)^5}$$

Design: $x_{in}=102$ ppm, $x_{out}=2$ ppm, so $1+\kappa=2.2$ per cell.

Interactive — follow the benzene

From 99.9 % to 2 ppm, and what breaks it

From the previous slide$x_{out}=x_{in}/(1+\kappa)^5$
Product benzene

Five times more benzene into R-103, or a bed at half activity, each brings the product to the 10 ppm spec — the finishing reactor has little spare capacity.

4 · The streams at design

The balances close

Mass balancet/h
Benzene in (1)34.80
Make-up gas in (11)2.98
Cyclohexane out (13)−37.52
Purge out (12)−0.28
Hydrogen balancekmol/h
Make-up H₂ in1419
Reacted (R-101 / R-102 / R-103)−1310 / −27 / −0.1
Lost in the purge−83

Section 4

What section 4 settled

  • Benzene meets hydrogen in R-101; the same gas then passes R-102 and R-103 in series.
  • R-101 cools by boil-up (E-103) and by the E-101 steam raiser.
  • V-104 splits 37.5 t/h of product from the recycle gas K-101 returns.
  • R-103 turns 100 ppm into 2 ppm with little spare capacity.

The streams are known. Section 5 shows the instruments and loops that hold them.

3 · The cascade

TIC-101 sets the flow, FIC-104 delivers it

The inner loop removes a flow disturbance before the reactor temperature has time to move.

Interactive — why cascade?

A pump-around disturbance with and without FIC-104

Peak rise, TIC → valve
Peak rise, TIC → FIC → valve

With the flow loop in between, the same disturbance barely moves R-101 — the fast inner loop absorbs what the slow outer loop would only see late.

4 · Selector switches

HEAT and COOL reverse the controller action

Switch positionE-101 shell (HS-101)TIC-101 actionHotter reactor…
COOL (normal)boiling water from D-101directopens FV-104: more cooling
HEAT (start-up)MP steam 184 °Creversecloses FV-104: less heating

TIC-102 and HS-102 on the R-102 jacket work the same way: HEAT is reverse acting, COOL is direct.

5 · Safety instrumented system (SIS)

Six trips and what a trip does

TripCauseDelay
TSHH-100R-101 temperature above 220 °C (independent element TT-100)5 s
TSHH-107any R-103 bed thermocouple above 220 °C5 s
PSHH-101R-101 pressure above 33.5 bar g3 s
XS-101 / XS-102agitator M-101 or compressor K-101 stopped while benzene is permitted10 s
LSHH-104V-104 level above 90 % → stops K-101 (then XS-102 trips)5 s

Trip action: XV-101 and XV-105 close, K-101 stops, E-101 to full cooling, R-102 jacket to COOL. ESD also opens EDV-101 to flare.

5 · Safety instrumented system

Permissives stop the two worst starts

Hydrogen (XV-105)

Only with loop oxygen AI-100 below 1 % — no flammable H₂/air mixture.

Benzene (XV-101)

Only into a reactor that is reset, gassed, pure enough, filled, mixed, hot and cooled — so no benzene accumulates.

Interactive — can benzene be permitted?

Tick what is true in the plant

XV-101 benzene

Each permissive blocks one route to a runaway — a missing one is a reason, not an obstacle.

5 · Safety instrumented system

The SIS tab in the simulator

State sequence, first-out, buttons (reset, admit H₂, permit benzene, EDV-101, ESD), live permissives and trip conditions.

Section 5

What section 5 settled

  • Tag letters give the measured variable, then the function.
  • Valves fail to the safe side: feed and hydrogen shut, cooling open.
  • TIC-101 drives FIC-104 so flow upsets never reach the reactor temperature.
  • HEAT and COOL reverse the temperature controllers’ action.
  • Six trips and two permissives stand between an upset and a runaway.

2 · The six DCS displays

Switch displays as you would on the console

Each display keeps the same drawing and shows the tags and calculations for one question — choose the display by the question you are asking.

3 · Bubbles and colours

Reading one instrument bubble

  • A red value is in alarm; a flashing one is not yet acknowledged.
  • Line colours: blue hydrocarbon, purple hydrogen, red steam, teal water.
  • Valves: green open, red closed, grey controlled with its opening beside it.

4 · Faceplates

Click a bubble: its faceplate opens

  • PV: the measured value. SP: the target. OUT: the valve signal, in %.
  • The bar shows PV on its range; the tick marks the set point.
  • Type a value and press Enter, or step with − / +.
  • The note explains what this loop is for and how it fails.

4 · Controller modes

MAN, AUTO and CAS

ModeYou setThe controller setsUse it when
MANOUTnothingstart-up, a failed transmitter
AUTOSPOUTnormal operation
CASnothingSP from its masterFIC-104 under TIC-101

Switching is bumpless: the output starts from where it was. While FIC-104 is not in CAS, TIC-101 tracks it.

Interactive — operate a flow loop

Switch modes and watch the valve

PV FIC-104

In AUTO the controller moves OUT to restore the flow after the disturbance; in MAN the flow stays wrong — a controller only helps in the mode that lets it act.

5 · Trends and alarms

Trend groups and the alarm summary

Trend panel

Seven groups: unit overview, R-101 cooling, R-102/R-103, hydrogen loop, steam, quality and money, or the selected tag (PV, SP, OUT). Window 5–60 min; each pen has its own range.

Alarm summary

Newest unacknowledged first. Clicking a row acknowledges it and opens its faceplate. Silence stops the horn only; the alarm keeps flashing until acknowledged.

Interactive — the life of one alarm

TIC-101 HI at 208 °C, with a deadband

The alarm clears only below 208 − 0.18 °C, so a noisy value near the limit does not chatter.

An alarm has four states, not two — acknowledging and clearing are separate events, and the log records both.

5 · The field

What only the outside operator can do

Equipment and valves

Start and stop pumps, agitator and K-101; open hand valves (N₂, vent, charge, catalyst, CW, MP steam); set selectors HS-101, HS-102, F-102, HS-115.

Checks, lab and telephone

Look, listen and read local gauges; samples return in 2 min; phone the hydrogen plant, utilities or tank farm.

What section 6 settled

  • Choose the display by the question: heat on Reactors, gas on Hydrogen loop, spec on R-103 and quality.
  • A bubble shows value, mode and alarm state at a glance.
  • MAN sets OUT, AUTO sets SP, CAS takes SP from a master.
  • Acknowledge, silence and clear are three different actions.

1 · Recycle compressor K-101

Compressor curve meets system curve

$\Delta P_c$
pressure rise K-101 delivers at flow $Q$
bar
$Q_d$
design flow, 46 000 Nm³/h
Nm³/h
$C_v$
FV-103 capacity × opening
—
$$\Delta P_c = a\,P_s\left[1-b\,(Q/Q_d)^2\right],\qquad \Delta P_{sys}=k\,(Q/Q_d)^2+(Q/C_v)^2$$

K-101: $a$ = 0.154, $b$ = 0.35 (falling head curve that scales with suction); $k$ = 1.0 bar for the reactor loop, plus the valve term.

Interactive — where does K-101 run?

FV-103 and suction pressure move the operating point

From the previous slide$\Delta P_c(Q)=\Delta P_{sys}(Q)$
Flow FIC-103
Discharge PI-112

Nearly closing FV-103 drives the flow toward zero and K-101 onto kickback; low suction pressure shrinks the whole curve — which is why K-101 is not started below 10 bar g.

2 · E-103 and V-103

The condenser sets how much R-101 can boil

$C_{cw}$
cooling-water flow × heat capacity
kW/K
$UA_3$
E-103 conductance, 500 kW/K
kW/K
$$Q_{max}=C_{cw}\left(1-e^{-UA_3/C_{cw}}\right)(T_{R101}-T_{cw})$$

Lose the water and $Q_{max}\to 0$: vapour blows through V-103 to R-102 (TI-103 jumps to ~200 °C).

3 · E-101 and D-101

Duty against the drum’s boiling point

$C$
pump-around flow × $c_p$
kW/K
$\varepsilon$
exchanger effectiveness, $1-e^{-UA/C}$
—
$T_{sat}(P_d)$
boiling temperature of water at drum pressure
°C
$$Q_{E101}=\varepsilon\,C\,\big(T_{R101}-T_{sat}(P_d)\big)$$

Design: 0.92 × 236 kW/K × (200 − 155.8) = 9.6 MW.

Interactive — the steam raiser

Flow, drum pressure and fouling against duty

From the previous slide$Q=\varepsilon C\,(T_{R101}-T_{sat})$
Drum boiling point $T_{sat}$
Effectiveness $\varepsilon$
E-101 duty
LP steam raised

R-101 held at 200 °C; the duty R-101 needs at design is 9.6 MW.

A higher drum pressure or a fouled tube bundle forces more pump-around for the same duty — so a rising FIC-104 at steady feed is a diagnostic signal.

4 · E-106 and V-104

Cool, separate, protect the compressor

E-106 product cooler

Cools the R-103 effluent 158 → 45 °C with cooling water, so the cyclohexane condenses and the recycle gas is dry.

V-104 HP separator

29 bar g; about 18 min of liquid at 50 % (LIC-104). LSHH-104 stops K-101 at 90 % so liquid never reaches it.

5 · Catalyst filter F-102

Filter pressure drop grows with the square of flow

$\Delta P_f$
filter pressure drop, PDI-102
bar
$c$
clogging factor, 1 when clean
—
$L$
liquid flow to R-103
kmol/s
$$\Delta P_f = R_f\,c\,L^2,\qquad R_f=55\ \mathrm{bar\,s^2/kmol^2}$$

P-102 and LV-102 supply about 3.7 bar in total; the filter takes an ever larger share.

Interactive — when does the filter starve R-103?

Clogging against the flow it can still pass

From the previous slide$\Delta P_f=R_f\,c\,L^2$
Max flow, LV-102 wide open
PDI-102 at 20.9 t/h (or the max)

Below about 21 t/h the R-102 level starts to rise; PDI-102 passes its 0.8 bar alarm long before — change filters on ΔP, not on level.

5 · Pumps

Three duties, each with a spare

PumpDutyIf it tripsProtect it from
P-100A/Bbenzene feedR-101 cools; restart feed gently—
P-101A/Bpump-around to E-101≈ 3 min to TSHH-100running dry below 20 % level
P-102A/BR-102 → filter → R-103R-102 level rises slowlyrunning dry below 8 % level

Section 7

What section 7 settled

  • K-101 runs where its curve meets the system curve; low suction or a closed FV-103 push it to kickback.
  • E-103’s cooling water caps R-101’s self-cooling.
  • E-101 duty falls when the drum pressure rises or the tubes foul.
  • V-104 level protects K-101; F-102 is changed on ΔP.

5 · Troubleshooting

Six stages, in order

StageYou produce
1 Engageis it dangerous? keep running, cut rate, isolate or shut down
2 Defineproblem statement with numbers, IS / IS NOT, target
3 Explorebalances and consistency checks, recent changes, causes
4 Planthree or more hypotheses, each with a test that could disprove it
5 Do itrun the tests, find the root cause, fix it, predict the response
6 Look backcompare prediction and result; propose a lasting change

Section 8

What section 8 settled

  • Six learning objectives drive 42 exercises of eight kinds.
  • Procedures are graded on safety, order, time and communication.
  • Training exercises teach one failure each; write your prediction first.
  • Troubleshooting follows six stages; EQUIPPED lists where to look.

Every exercise uses the same few equations and loops — go back to Sections 1 and 5 when a trend surprises you.

Closing

Key Takeaways

1

Remove 2.6 GJ per tonne of benzene: E-101 plus boil-up, every minute.

2

Keep R-101 at 195–205 °C: MCP above, benzene slip below.

3

Watch $p_{H_2}=(P-P_{sat})\,y_{H_2}$: pressure, temperature and purge set the rate.

4

Never feed benzene to a reactor that cannot react it at once.

5

Close the hydrogen balance to find leaks and lost conversion.
